title: Refused building consent: custom fixed glazing system on a proposed two-storey house (Auckland)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE Chief Executive determination; Building Act 2004; comparative only, not Alberta)
code_edition: NZ Building Code, First Schedule, Building Regulations 1992 (cited in s1.3); verification-method and acceptable-solution editions not stated in the extracted text
document_type: MBIE Chief Executive determination 2018/040 (PDF, 20 pages, Building Act 2004 s177/s188)

facts.text: Proposed two-storey house in an Extra High wind zone; cladding is vertical shiplap cedar weatherboards with fixed glazing panels; upper floor is cross-laminated timber walls and floors on concrete piles and retaining walls.

Fixed glazing was intended for all elevations, with panels 3.0 to 3.8 m high and 1.0 to 2.4 m wide; the glazing manufacturer designed the insulated units and structural sealant bite; the applicant designed the joinery and fixings.

Consent drawings show a proprietary silicone sealant on polyethylene-foam rod at the glazing edges; the producer statement PS1 from the glazing manufacturer covers structural tape and structural silicone.

Figure 1 shows the elevations with the fixed glazing (p.2); Figure 2 is a head and sill detail of the original system (p.3). The PDF embeds consent elevation sheet A1-011 at 1:100 and a junction detail with dimensions (viewed as extracted images).
facts.locator: p.2 Fig.1; p.3 Fig.2; embedded images p.2 and p.4

facts.text: A WANZ weathertightness test was run on a scaled version with vertical timber cladding and photographs of the test are included; the determination notes the test is not designed to assess facade prototypes.
